title: Yesterday
description: Say what you did, and who you did it with.

explanation.summary: The preterite is the tense for something that happened and is finished. With -ar verbs it is almost entirely regular, and the one irregular part is the yo form.

sections.heading: The endings
sections.body: The -ar preterite has its own set of endings: -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron. They are not the same as the present endings, which is why the tense is easy to spot. Hablar becomes hablé, hablaste, habló, hablamos, hablasteis, hablaron.

examples.en: Yesterday I spoke to my mother.

sections.heading: The yo form
sections.body: The yo form takes an accent, and for most verbs it is the infinitive with the final vowel changed to é. But some verbs change their stem instead: tener becomes tuve, estar became estuviste, poder became pude, hacer became hice, ir and ser became fui, and estar and tener also have irregular third person forms: estuvo, tuvo.

sections.heading: When you use it
sections.body: The preterite belongs to a finished period: ayer, la semana pasada, en 2020, hace dos años. It is also what you use when something interrupts another past action: dormía cuando sonó el teléfono, I was sleeping when the phone rang. The phone rang is the interruption, so it takes the preterite.

examples.en: Last year I travelled a lot.
I was sleeping when the phone rang.
